newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch money market rates edge lower.
newsitem.headline: Dutch money market rates edge lower.

text.p: Dutch money market rates edged lower on Wednesday and call money rates were stable at their recent high level.
Dealers said the market was calm, with the US Federal Reserve rate hike of 25 basis points within expectations.
Dealers expected the Dutch new special advances pact at 1500 GMT to remain at 2.90 percent.
Meanwhile, the guilder lost some ground versus the mark.
The guilder was somewhat stronger on Tuesday and dealers said it would have to rise closer to 112.00 per 100 marks before the Dutch central bank eased rates.

Earlier this month, the central bank raised the special advances rate by 20 basis points to 2.90 percent and the secured loans rate by 50 basis points to 2.50 percent, because the guilder had become weaker versus the mark.
The guilder was trading at 112.50 per 100 marks today versus 112.43 on Tuesday.
The Dutch currency was lingering near 112.60 when the Dutch central bank hiked rates.
Call money rates were stable, trading between 3.06-3.12 bid.
One-month deposits slipped two basis points to 3.10 percent bid and six-month paper was bid at 3.22 percent bid versus 3.24 percent.
